properties.formattedContent:
Question: can you get booster shot after covid

Answer: Yes, it is recommended to get an updated COVID-19 booster at least 2 months after your last COVID-19 shot, or 3 months after having COVID-19. This updated vaccine helps your immune system recognize the currently circulating COVID-19 strains. According to the CDC, you should get the updated vaccine when it is available to you to reduce your risk of symptomatic infection.

0.fact: it is recommended to get an updated COVID-19 booster at least 2 months after your last COVID-19 shot
0.explanation: CDC guidance for the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine recommends a minimum interval of 2 months after the last COVID-19 vaccine dose before receiving an additional dose, especially for immunocompromised individuals and booster doses[2][4].

1.fact: it is recommended to get an updated COVID-19 booster at least 3 months after having COVID-19
1.explanation: While the exact timing can vary, CDC guidance generally recommends waiting about 3 months after a COVID-19 infection before getting a booster to optimize immune response and avoid overlap with natural immunity. This is consistent with clinical guidance to space vaccination and infection by about 3 months, though specific intervals may vary by individual risk and vaccine formulation[2].

2.fact: This updated vaccine helps your immune system recognize the currently circulating COVID-19 strains
2.explanation: The FDA and CDC have updated COVID-19 vaccines to include components targeting currently circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., the 2025-2026 monovalent JN.1-lineage vaccine) to improve immune recognition and protection against prevalent strains[1].

3.fact: According to the CDC, you should get the updated vaccine when it is available to you to reduce your risk of symptomatic infection
3.explanation: CDC recommends receiving the updated COVID-19 vaccine as soon as it is available to reduce the risk of symptomatic infection and severe outcomes, especially for those at higher risk[2][3].
